html:
Khosrow I, called Anushirvan, "of the immortal soul", was king of kings of the Sasanian Empire of Iran from 531 to 579. He is remembered in Persian and Arabic tradition as the model of a just and wise ruler.

He came to the throne after his father Kavad I and a bloody crushing of the Mazdakite movement. He then rebuilt the state: land was surveyed and taxed at fixed rates, the army was paid by the state, and the empire was split into four military commands. Great works such as the Nahrawan Canal are credited to him.

His long contest with Justinian shaped the century:

  • 532: the Perpetual Peace, bought with Roman gold.
  • 540: he broke it, sacked Antioch and settled its people in a new city near Ctesiphon.
  • 541 to 562: the Lazic War over Lazica on the Black Sea, ended by the Fifty-Year Peace.

In the east, around 560, he and the Türks together destroyed the Hephthalites. Around 570 he sent a force to drive the Aksumites out of Yemen.

His court was open to learning. Greek philosophers who left Athens after Justinian closed its schools stayed with him for a time. Indian books were put into Middle Persian, among them the fables later known as Kalila and Dimna, and tradition says chess reached Persia in his reign.
sum: Khosrow I, called Anushirvan, "of the immortal soul", was king of kings of the Sasanian Empire of Iran from 531 to 579. He is remembered in Persian and Arabic tradition as the model of a just and wise ruler.
